messages:
maya: quick heads-up — canary-6 (rv3-kernel-swap) is showing a notable regression in prefix cache primary_hit_rate for chat workloads. first-token latency up ~30ms and overall primary hit rate dropped ~12%. anyone else on canary seeing this?

tom: saw the alert on the dashboard. which workloads are affected? chat only or completions/RAG as well?

maya: mostly chat flows and structured-output prompts. RAG retrieval prompts look stable. short completions unaffected. the impact is pronounced for long-context chats (>2k tokens) where hit rate fell off a cliff.

ash: my first thought is keying divergence. the kernel swap changed execution ordering and we landed a minor change to how convo metadata is serialized into cache keys (reordered fields). could be nondeterministic JSON ordering.
\nmaria: can you paste a telemetry snippet for a missed prefix so we can diff computed keys between hits and misses?

maya: pasted below (redacted):

```
[2026-03-10T15:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-xl-13b kernel=rv3 quant=int8 convo_prefix="{\"user\": \"I have a bug\", \"context\": {\"files\": [{\"name\": \"main.py\", \"path\": \"/repo/src\"}]}}" cache_key=kwf:sha1:0x7a9f... hit=false
[2026-03-10T15:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 computed_key=sha1(sorted-json(prefix)) => 0x7a9f...
[2026-03-10T15:12:03Z] cache_lookup_time_ms=0.6 prefix_match=false kv_prefetch=false
```

ash: curious that computed_key shows sorted-json but the actual lookup fingerprint differs sometimes. suggests certain code paths still use raw-string hashing instead of canonicalized fingerprints.

devx: recall a small perf PR that added a fast-path to avoid JSON serialization on hot paths; it defers canonicalization to miss handling. if two requests take different paths we end up with distinct keys for the same logical prefix -> fragmentation.

maya: exactly. when one request uses the fast-path (raw chunk digest) and another uses canonicalized JSON fingerprint we get two fingerprints for the same prefix, splitting hits. that matches the telemetry pattern.

tom: explains why structured chat is hit more — convo metadata often contains arrays or tool outputs where key order isn't stable. plain text completions unaffected.

maria: mitigation options: (1) enforce deterministic canonicalization at the entrypoint for every request, or (2) background rekeyer that normalizes KV entries and merges counters. both tradeoffs are real.

ash: full canonicalize per-request costs ~0.5ms CPU on hot paths but fixes fragmentation. background rekeyer is complex: scans DB, merges entries, handles counts/ttl, and risks race conditions.

devx: consider hybrid: keep fast-path for short text prefixes, and implement a json-aware deterministic hash for JSON-like prefixes that's fast and stable.

maya: telemetry shows ~70% of misses are minor structural diffs (whitespace, key order, ephemeral trace IDs). if we can strip ephemeral keys and stable-sort JSON only when prefix looks JSON-ish we might recover most hits without paying full canonicalization cost.

tom: propose json-aware canonicalizer algorithm:
- detect JSON-like prefix (starts with '{' or '[')
- remove ephemeral keys by regex (trace_id|request_id|timestamp)
- recursively sort object keys
- minify whitespace
This keeps CPU lower than a generic heavy canonicalizer.

maria: i'll run a repro against canary. please drop a reproducible script and target metrics.

maya: repro script below. it interleaves 500 chat messages that are logically identical but serialized differently to emulate client variability. measure prefix_primary_hit_rate before/after.

```
# simplified repro (bash)
for i in `seq 1 500`; do
  payload=$(jq -n --arg u "I have a bug" --arg id "$RANDOM" '{user:$u,context:{files:[{name:"main.py",path:"/repo/src"}],meta:{trace_id:$id}}}')
  curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"prefix\":$payload, \"model\":\"redwood-xl-13b\"}" &
done
wait

# then query telemetry
curl -sS "https://canary.redwood/internal/telemetry?metric=prefix_primary_hit_rate&since=10m" | jq .
```

ash: also add unit tests that exercise both fast-path and canonicalize path. ci should catch divergence by comparing fingerprints for a seeded set of prefixes.

devx: agreed. immediate actions: rollback fast-path on canary, add json-aware canonicalizer + unit tests, run the repro, and if hit-rate recovers reintroduce fast-path behind heuristic gating.

maya: rolling back fast-path now. patch: `git revert r12345` — rolling deploy.

maria: i'll start the repro and share dashboards. baseline target primary_hit_rate ~88% for long chat; canary currently ~76%. target after fix >85%.

tom: add a perf counter labeled keying_path with values {fastpath, canonical, json_aware} so we can attribute misses/hits.

ash: logging reminder: never log full prefixes in prod. store only redactable fingerprints and link to ephemeral sample storage for deeper debugging.

devx: good call. add PII sanitization step before any sample export.

maya: thanks all. i'll update when rollback completes and telemetry shows improvement. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-rollback r12345 started on cluster canary-6 by maya. ETA ~2m.
